title: White Pizza with Cheese and Vegetables, Thin Crust

content.title: About
content.content: White pizza with cheese and vegetables on a thin crust is a lighter version of the classic pizza that skips the tomato sauce. Instead, a creamy base made from mozzarella, parmesan and cream is used, topped with fresh vegetables such as bell pepper, zucchini, mushrooms, spinach and onion. The thin, crispy crust highlights the delicate cheese flavor and the freshness of the veggies.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: White pizza originated in Italy as an alternative to the traditional red pizza, replacing tomato sauce with a creamy cheese sauce.
The thin crust is often made without yeast, resulting in a crispier and lower‑calorie base.
The combination of mozzarella and parmesan gives the pizza a distinctive buttery aroma and a subtle sharpness.
The vegetables used are rich in vitamins A, C and K as well as antioxidants.
In some regions the pizza is finished with a drizzle of olive oil and fresh basil to enhance flavor.

items.title: Rich source of calcium
items.content: The cheeses in the white pizza provide a high amount of calcium, essential for bone and teeth health.

items.title: Vitamins and minerals from vegetables
items.content: Bell pepper, spinach and zucchini supply vitamins A, C, K and potassium, supporting immunity and heart function.

items.title: Low in added sugar
items.content: The absence of tomato sauce and added sugars makes this pizza more suitable for blood‑glucose management.

items.title: Protein‑rich
items.content: Mozzarella and parmesan deliver a complete set of essential amino acids for tissue repair.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: A thin crust made from whole‑grain flour adds dietary fiber, promoting regular bowel movements.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: The cheeses may cause discomfort for people who are lactose intolerant.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Cheese and added salt can increase sodium intake, which is a concern for hypertension.

items.title: Dairy allergy
items.content: Individuals allergic to milk proteins (casein) should avoid this pizza.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Despite the thin crust, the cheese sauce makes the dish relatively calorie‑dense; portion control is advised.

items.title: Gluten
items.content: The crust contains gluten, so the pizza is not suitable for those with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Slice the pizza into serving pieces and enjoy it hot, straight from the oven. Fresh basil or arugula can be added for extra aroma. A light drizzle of olive oil or balsamic glaze is optional.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2‑3 days. Reheat in an oven or grill to restore the crisp crust. For longer storage, freeze whole portions wrapped tightly in plastic film.
